homes.area_note: Sales are tied to Bellevue through OTR assessment sub-areas Congress Heights A and C in OTR's Integrated Tax System Public Extract, not through the DC Health planning-area boundary used elsewhere on this site, because the tax extract has no coordinates. The two areas overlap but do not match exactly. Fit with the Bellevue boundary, measured this run by tax square (a square counts as inside if any DC address point on it falls inside the DC Health polygon, so edge squares make these upper bounds; measured 2026-11-06): 64% of the 2,419 house and condo parcels in the OTR area(s) sit on squares inside the boundary, and 79% of house and condo parcels on in-boundary squares belong to the OTR area(s).
homes.sales_note: Only deeds OTR codes "Market Sale" at $75,000 or more are counted (same filter as the prototypes); foreclosures, buyer=seller transfers, speculative, tax-deed, unusual and multi-parcel sales are excluded. "house" = row, semi-detached and detached (use codes 011-013); "condo" = use codes 016-017. Dates are deed sale dates; deeds reach the extract a few weeks after closing, so the newest weeks undercount. The extract keeps only each parcel's most recent sale, so a home that resold within 24 months counts once, in its later window. "Assessed" is OTR's current total assessment (NEWTOTAL), which may postdate the sale. Building area and bedrooms are from CAMA Residential (houses only).
homes.by_month_basis: houses only; calendar months, the last one in progress; median null when under 3 sales

trees.empty_boxes_note: Counted from the layer's tree-box status (TBOX_STAT). 'Open' = an empty box ready to plant (101). Not counted: 'Proposed' = planting scheduled (5), 'Conflict'/'Utility' = empty but blocked (108), 'Retired' = box removed (124). 'total' is boxes with status 'Plant' whose condition is not Dead.

streets.service_note: Median days from request to closure for requests opened in the last 12 months and already closed, computed from request and resolution timestamps only (exact here; citywide from server-side quantiles). When the window spans two yearly layers the citywide median is merged from each layer's quantiles (accurate to a few percent). Requests still open are excluded, which biases recent months toward faster closes, equally here and citywide.

featured_block.sentence: In 1941, D. C. Engineering Co. built 43 buildings on the 4000 block of 1st Street SW under 3 permits, designed by A. H. Sonnemann and George S. brock. The largest permit covered 24 buildings at an estimated $72,000 in total.

archive.note: No usable mentions in the Evening Star for October 31 – November 6, 1926 (2 matching pages searched). Some weeks a neighborhood just isn't in the paper. Clips are machine-read text (OCR) from scanned Evening Star pages on the Library of Congress's Chronicling America, lightly cleaned (line-break hyphens rejoined, stray symbols removed); misspellings are the scanner's. Newspapers this old are public domain. Each clip links to its page at loc.gov. Clips that mention race, covenants, deed restrictions or slurs are skipped automatically (keyword list: race, races, racial, colored, coloured, negro, negroes, white only, whites only, for whites, white people, white persons, white residents, caucasian, segregation, segregated, covenant, covenants, restricted, restriction, restrictions, plus a list of slurs), because they need an editor's context; legal notices and lists of private individuals are skipped too.
